Lesson 01 · A private conversation

问题
Why did the writer complain to the people behind him?
作者为什么向他后面的人抱怨？
Why/waɪ/为什么（疑问副词）did/dɪd/（助动词，构成疑问句）the/ðə/（定冠词，不译）writer/ˈraɪtə/作者complain/kəmˈpleɪn/抱怨to/tə/向（介词）the/ðə/（定冠词，不译）people/ˈpiːpəl/人们behind/bɪˈhaɪnd/在……后面（介词）him?/hɪm/他？

Last week I went to the theatre. I had a very good seat. The play was very interesting. I did not enjoy it. A young man and a young woman were sitting behind me. They were talking loudly. I got very angry.
上星期我去看戏。我的座位非常好。这出戏很有意思，可我却没能欣赏。一个年轻男子和一个年轻女子坐在我后面，他们在大声说话。我非常生气。

正文
I could not hear the actors. I turned round. I looked at the man and the woman angrily. They did not pay any attention. In the end, I could not bear it. I turned round again. 'I can't hear a word!' I said angrily.
我听不见演员说话。我转过身，气愤地看着那个男子和那个女子。他们毫不理会。最后，我实在受不了了。我又转过身去。‘我一个字也听不见！’我气愤地说。

Lesson 02 · Breakfast or lunch？

问题
Why was the writer's aunt surprised?
作者的姑妈为什么感到惊讶？
Why/waɪ/为什么（疑问副词）was/wɒz/是the/ðə/（定冠词，不译）writer's/ˈraɪtəz/作者的aunt/ɑːnt/姑妈surprised?/səˈpraɪzd/感到惊讶？

It was Sunday. I never get up early on Sundays. I sometimes stay in bed until lunchtime. Last Sunday I got up very late. I looked out of the window. It was dark outside. 'What a day!' I thought. 'It's raining again.'
那天是星期天。星期天我从不起早。我有时会在床上一直躺到午饭时间。上个星期天我起得很晚。我向窗外望去，外面天色昏暗。‘多糟的一天！’我心想。‘又下雨了。’

正文
Just then, the telephone rang. It was my aunt Lucy. 'I've just arrived by train,' she said. 'I'm coming to see you.' 'But I'm still having breakfast,' I said. 'What are you doing?' she asked. 'I'm having breakfast,' I repeated.
就在这时，电话铃响了。是我露西姑妈。‘我刚乘火车到，’她说。‘我这就来看你。’‘可我还在吃早饭呢，’我说。‘你在干什么？’她问。‘我在吃早饭，’我又说了一遍。
Just then,/dʒʌst ðen/就在这时，the/ðə/（定冠词，不译）telephone/ˈtelɪˌfəʊn/电话rang./ræŋ/响（过去式）。It/ɪt/（指代打电话的人）was/wɒz/是my/maɪ/我的aunt Lucy./ɑːnt ˈluːsi/露西姑妈。'I've/aɪv/‘我（I have 的缩写，构成完成时）just/dʒʌst/刚arrived/əˈraɪvd/到达（过去分词）by/baɪ/乘（介词，表方式）train,'/treɪn/火车，’she/ʃiː/她said./sed/说（过去式）。'I'm/aɪm/‘我（I am 的缩写）coming/ˈkʌmɪŋ/来（现在分词）to/tə/（不定式符号，不译）see/siː/看you.'/juː/你。’'But/bʌt/‘但I'm/aɪm/我（I am 的缩写）still/stɪl/还having/ˈhævɪŋ/吃（现在分词）breakfast,'/ˈbrekfəst/早饭，’I/aɪ/我said./sed/说（过去式）。'What/wɒt/‘什么（疑问词）are/ɑː/（助动词，构成进行时）you/juː/你doing?'/ˈduːɪŋ/做（现在分词）？’she/ʃiː/她asked./ɑːskt/问（过去式）。'I'm/aɪm/‘我（I am 的缩写）having/ˈhævɪŋ/吃（现在分词）breakfast,'/ˈbrekfəst/早饭，’I/aɪ/我repeated./rɪˈpiːtɪd/重复说（过去式）。

'Dear me,' she said. 'Do you always get up so late? It's one o'clock!'

Lesson 03 · Please send me a card

问题
How many cards did the writer send?
作者寄出了多少张明信片？
How many/haʊ ˈmeni/多少（疑问词）cards/kɑːdz/明信片did/dɪd/（助动词，构成疑问句）the/ðə/（定冠词，不译）writer/ˈraɪtə/作者send?/send/寄？
正文
Postcards always spoil my holidays. Last summer, I went to Italy. I visited museums and sat in public gardens. A friendly waiter taught me a few words of Italian. Then he lent me a book.
明信片总是让我的假日不得安宁。去年夏天，我去了意大利。我参观了博物馆，还在公园里闲坐。一位友好的服务员教了我几句意大利语。后来他借给我一本书。
Postcards/ˈpəʊstkɑːdz/明信片always/ˈɔːlweɪz/总是spoil/spɔɪl/搅乱my/maɪ/我的holidays./ˈhɒlɪˌdeɪz/假日。Last/lɑːst/去年summer,/ˈsʌmə/夏天，I/aɪ/我went/went/去（过去式）to/tə/到（介词）Italy./ˈɪtəli/意大利。I/aɪ/我visited/ˈvɪzɪtɪd/参观（过去式）museums/mjuːˈzɪəmz/博物馆and/ænd/和sat/sæt/坐（过去式）in/ɪn/在public gardens./ˈpʌblɪk ˈɡɑːdənz/公园。A/ə/一个friendly/ˈfrendli/友好的waiter/ˈweɪtə/服务员taught/tɔːt/教（过去式）me/miː/我a few/ə fjuː/几words/wɜːdz/词of/ɒv/的Italian./ɪˈtæliən/意大利语。Then/ðen/后来he/hiː/他lent/lent/借给（过去式）me/miː/我a/ə/一本book./bʊk/书。
正文
I read a few lines, but I did not understand a word. Every day I thought about postcards. My holidays passed quickly, but I did not send cards to my friends. On the last day I made a big decision.
我读了几行，却一个字也看不懂。我天天惦记着明信片。我的假期很快过去了，但我没有给朋友们寄明信片。最后一天，我下了一个大决心。
I/aɪ/我read/red/读（过去式）a few/ə fjuː/几lines,/laɪnz/行，but/bʌt/但I/aɪ/我did/dɪd/（助动词，构成否定）not/nɒt/不understand/ˌʌndəˈstænd/理解a/ə/一个word./wɜːd/字。Every day/ˈevri deɪ/每天I/aɪ/我thought about/θɔːt əˈbaʊt/惦记（过去式）postcards./ˈpəʊstkɑːdz/明信片。My/maɪ/我的holidays/ˈhɒlɪˌdeɪz/假期passed/pɑːst/过去（过去式）quickly,/ˈkwɪkli/很快，but/bʌt/但I/aɪ/我did/dɪd/（助动词，构成否定）not/nɒt/不send/send/寄cards/kɑːdz/明信片to/tə/给（介词）my/maɪ/我的friends./frendz/朋友们。On/ɒn/在the/ðə/（定冠词，不译）last/lɑːst/最后day/deɪ/天I/aɪ/我made/meɪd/做（过去式）a/ə/一个big/bɪɡ/大的decision./dɪˈsɪʒən/决定。

Lesson 04 · An exciting trip

问题
Why is Tim finding this trip exciting?
蒂姆为什么觉得这次旅行令人兴奋？
Why/waɪ/为什么（疑问副词）is/ɪz/（助动词，构成现在进行时）Tim/tɪm/蒂姆finding/ˈfaɪndɪŋ/觉得（现在分词）this/ðɪs/这次trip/trɪp/旅行exciting?/ekˈsaɪtɪŋ/令人兴奋？

I have just received a letter from my brother, Tim. He is in Australia. He has been there for six months. Tim is an engineer. He is working for a big firm and he has already visited a great number of different places in Australia.
我刚收到哥哥蒂姆的一封来信。他在澳大利亚，在那里已经待了六个月。蒂姆是一名工程师，正在为一家大公司工作，而且已经游览了澳大利亚许多不同的地方。

正文

'Certainly,' the girl said, 'but they're for next Wednesday's performance. Do you still want them?' 'I might as well have them,' I said sadly.

Lesson 20 · One man in a boat

I never catch anything—not even old boots. After having spent whole mornings on the river, I always go home with an empty bag. 'You must give up fishing!' my friends say. 'It's a waste of time.'

Lesson 22 · A glass envelope

Lesson 48 · Did you want to tell me something？

He knew I collected match boxes and asked me whether my collection was growing. He then asked me how my brother was and whether I liked my new job in London. In answer to these questions I either nodded or made strange noises.

He suggested that a double railway-tunnel should be built. This would solve the problem of ventilation, for if a train entered this tunnel, it would draw in fresh air behind it. Forty-two years later a tunnel was actually begun.

Why does Tazieff risk his life like this?

The driver gave him a few biscuits and a cup of coffee and left him just outside the city. The next car the boy stopped did not take him into the centre of Paris as he hoped it would, but to Perpignan on the French-Spanish border.

Lesson 75 · SOS

他们还发现了一样 X 光片没有显示出来的东西：一个杜阿穆特夫神的小蜡像。这位长着牛头的神通常被安放在木乃伊内。医生们尚未确定那位妇女的死因。

Lesson 78 · The last one？

问题
For how long did the writer give up smoking?

After reading an article entitled 'Cigarette Smoking and Your Health' I lit a cigarette to calm my nerves. I smoked with concentration and pleasure as I was sure that this would be my last cigarette.
读完一篇题为‘吸烟与你的健康’的文章之后，我点了一支烟来镇定神经。我聚精会神而又愉快地抽着，因为我确信这将是我的最后一支烟。

For a whole week I did not smoke at all and during this time, my wife suffered terribly. I had all the usual symptoms of someone giving up smoking: a bad temper and an enormous appetite.

My friends kept on offering me cigarettes and cigars. They made no effort to hide their amusement whenever I produced a packet of sweets from my pocket. After seven days of this I went to a party.
我的朋友们不停地给我递香烟和雪茄。每当我一从口袋里掏出一包糖果，他们也毫不掩饰自己的乐趣。这样过了七天之后，我去参加了一个聚会。

Everybody around me was smoking and I felt extremely uncomfortable. When my old friend Brian urged me to accept a cigarette, it was more than I could bear. I took one guiltily, lit it and smoked with satisfaction.
我周围的每个人都在抽烟，我感到极不自在。当我的老朋友布赖恩劝我接一支烟时，我再也受不了了。我内疚地接了一支，点上，心满意足地抽了起来。

My wife was delighted that things had returned to normal once more. Anyway, as Brian pointed out, it is the easiest thing in the world to give up smoking. He himself has done it lots of times!
我妻子很高兴，一切又恢复了正常。不管怎样，正如布赖恩所指出的，戒烟是世上最容易的事。他本人就干过好多次！

Later we learnt that there was a very important person on board. The police had been told that a bomb had been planted on the plane. After we had landed, the plane was searched thoroughly.
后来我们得知，机上有一位非常重要的人物。警方此前已得到消息，这架飞机上被人安放了一枚炸弹。我们着陆之后，飞机被彻底搜查了一遍。

正文
Fortunately, nothing was found and five hours later we were able to take off again.
幸运的是，什么也没发现，五小时后我们才得以再次起飞。

回答
Answer: Because the police had been told that a bomb had been planted on the plane, it turned back to be searched.

Perhaps the most extraordinary building of the nineteenth century was the Crystal Palace, which was built in Hyde Park for the Great Exhibition of 1851.

The Crystal Palace was different from all other buildings in the world, for it was made of iron and glass. It was one of the biggest buildings of all time and a lot of people from many countries came to see it.
水晶宫与世界上所有其他建筑都不同，因为它是由钢铁和玻璃建成的。它是有史以来最大的建筑之一，来自许多国家的大批人前来参观。

正文
A great many goods were sent to the exhibition from various parts of the world. There was also a great deal of machinery on display. The most wonderful piece of machinery on show was Nasmyth's steam hammer.
许多商品从世界各地被送往博览会。展出的还有大量机械。展出中最奇妙的一件机械是内史密斯的蒸汽锤。

Though in those days, travelling was not as easy as it is today, steam boats carried thousands of visitors across the Channel from Europe. On arriving in England, they were taken to the Crystal Palace by train.
尽管在那个年代，旅行不像今天这样容易，汽船还是把成千上万的参观者从欧洲运过了英吉利海峡。一到达英国，他们便乘火车被送往水晶宫。

There were six million visitors in all, and the profits from the exhibition were used to build museums and colleges. Later, the Crystal Palace was moved to South London.

Lesson 81 · Escape

战俘为什么要袭击司机？

When he had killed the guard, the prisoner of war quickly dragged him into the bushes. Working rapidly in the darkness, he soon changed into the dead man's clothes.
战俘杀死卫兵后，迅速把他拖进了灌木丛。他在黑暗中动作麻利，很快就换上了死者的衣服。

Now, dressed in a blue uniform and with a rifle over his shoulder, the prisoner marched boldly up and down in front of the camp. He could hear shouting in the camp itself.
这时，他穿着蓝色军服，肩上挎着步枪，大胆地在营地前来回走动。他能听到营区里面传来的喊叫声。

Lights were blazing and men were running here and there: they had just discovered that a prisoner had escaped. At that moment, a large black car with four officers inside it, stopped at the camp gates.

The officers got out and the prisoner stood to attention and saluted as they passed. When they had gone, the driver of the car came towards him. The man obviously wanted to talk.

He was rather elderly with grey hair and clear blue eyes. The prisoner felt sorry for him, but there was nothing else he could do. As the man came near, the prisoner knocked him to the ground with a sharp blow.

Answer: Because he wanted to steal the car and escape — he knocked the driver down, jumped into the car and drove off.

The same policeman was just walking slowly past the entrance, when Patrick asked the same question. Though a little suspicious this time, the policeman gave him the same answer.

The day after, Patrick went to the house once more and asked exactly the same question. This time, the policeman lost his temper.

'I told you yesterday and the day before yesterday,' he shouted, 'Mr. Lane was defeated in the elections. He has retired from political life and gone to live abroad!' 'I know,' answered Patrick, 'but I love to hear you say it!'

So it comes as a surprise to learn that giant fish are terrifying the divers on North Sea oil rigs.
因此，得知巨型鱼正在吓着北海石油钻井平台上的潜水员，着实令人意外。

Oil rigs have to be repaired frequently and divers, who often have to work in darkness a hundred feet under water, have been frightened out of their wits by giant fish bumping into them as they work.
石油钻井平台不得不经常维修，而潜水员常常要在水下一百英尺的黑暗中作业，作业时撞上他们的巨型鱼一直把他们吓得魂不附体。

Now they have had special cages made to protect them from these monsters.

正文
The fish are not sharks or killer whales, but favourite eating varieties like cod and skate which grow to unnatural sizes, sometimes as much as twelve feet in length.
这些鱼不是鲨鱼，也不是虎鲸，而是像鳕鱼和鳐鱼这类人们常吃的品种，它们长到不正常的个头，有时身长多达十二英尺。

正文
Three factors have caused these fish to grow so large: the warm water round the hot oil pipes under the sea; the plentiful supply of food thrown overboard by the crews on the rigs;
有三个因素使这些鱼长得如此之大：海底灼热的输油管周围温暖的海水；平台上的工人从平台边扔下的充足食物；

正文
the total absence of fishing boats around the oil rigs. As a result, the fish just eat and eat and grow and grow in the lovely warm water. Who eats who?
钻井平台周围完全见不到渔船。结果，这些鱼就在可爱的温暖海水里一味地吃呀吃、长呀长。谁吃谁？

Answer: They are cod and skate — favourite eating fish which have grown to unnatural sizes in the warm water around the oil rigs.

I tried to wake up my wife by ringing the doorbell, but she was fast asleep, so I got a ladder from the shed in the garden, put it against the wall, and began climbing towards the bedroom window.

'Excuse my interrupting you. I hate to interrupt a man when he's busy working, but would you mind coming with me to the station?' 'Well, I'd prefer to stay here,' I said. 'You see, I've forgotten my key.' 'Your what?' he called.
‘请原谅我打断你。我不愿打扰一个正忙着干活的人，可你介意跟我去一趟警察局吗？’‘嗯，我宁愿待在这儿，’我说。‘你知道，我忘带钥匙了。’‘你什么？’他喊道。

Lesson 94 · Future champions

问题
What kind of race do the children compete in?
孩子们参加的是哪种比赛？
What kind of/wɒt kaɪnd ɒv/哪种race/reɪs/比赛do/duː/（助动词，构成疑问句）the/ðə/（定冠词，不译）children/ˈtʃɪldrən/孩子们compete in?/kəmˈpiːt ɪn/参加？
正文
Experiments have proved that children can be instructed in swimming at a very early age. At a special swimming pool in Los Angeles, children become expert at holding their breath under water even before they can walk.

A Festival for the Dead is held once a year in Japan. This festival is a cheerful occasion, for on this day, the dead are said to return to their homes and they are welcomed by the living.
在日本，亡灵节每年举行一次。这个节日是个欢乐的场合，因为据说在这一天，死者会回到家中，受到生者的欢迎。

正文
As they are expected to be hungry after their long journey, food is laid out for them. Specially-made lanterns are hung outside each house to help the dead to find their way. All night long, people dance and sing.
人们认为他们长途跋涉之后一定饿了，于是为他们摆好食物。各家门外挂着特制的灯笼，帮助死者找到回家的路。人们通宵达旦地跳舞唱歌。

正文
In the early morning, the food that had been laid out for the dead is thrown into a river or into the sea as it is considered unlucky for anyone living to eat it.
清晨，先前为死者摆好的食物被扔进河里或海里，因为活人吃这些食物被认为是不吉利的。

正文
In towns that are near the sea, the tiny lanterns which had been hung in the streets the night before, are placed into the water when the festival is over.
在靠海的城镇，前一天晚上挂在街上的小灯笼，在节日结束时被放入水中。

正文
Thousands of lanterns slowly drift out to sea guiding the dead on their return journey to the other world.
成千上万的灯笼缓缓漂向大海，为死者指引着返回另一个世界的路。

正文
This is a moving spectacle, for crowds of people stand on the shore watching the lanterns drifting away until they can be seen no more.
这是一幅动人的景象，因为成群的人站在岸边，看着灯笼渐渐漂远，直到再也看不见。

回答
Answer: They are placed into the water and slowly drift out to sea, guiding the dead on their return journey to the other world.
答案：它们被放入水中，缓缓漂向大海，为死者指引着返回另一个世界的路。
